articles.title: Separating Fact From Fiction In Netflix's New True Crime Drama The Altruists
articles.description: This article contains spoilers for Netflix’s The Altruists Nothing makes Netflix audiences happier than watching a juicy true crime series. Earlier this week, the streamer brought us another stranger-than-fiction drama, this time about the so-called Bitcoin Bonnie and Clyde, Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison. The Altruists follows the MIT graduates who had one professional goal, to make billions while giving away a significant amount to charity. Over its eight episodes, the show tracks the rise and collapse of the pair’s cryptocurrency exchange and eventual imprisonment. Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner in Netflix's true crime drama The Altruists When putting together The Altruists, showrunner Graham Moore drew inspiration from transcripts from the couple’s trials, interviews and leaked recordings – but, like any drama that’s based on a true story, artistic liberties were also taken with the characters and the factual events. “I can never prove what was going on in the hearts or minds of Sam’s friends when they made those decisions,” Graham Moore told Business Insider. “But I could do a ton of research on their lives and their backgrounds, and what was going on, and look at what they’ve said publicly – those people who’ve been able to say things publicly – and ask myself, ‘OK, what do I think happened here? What can I imagine could have driven these fractures?’” So, what actually went down in real life and what did the showrunner just make up for the audiences at home? Here’s a quick guide to the true story behind the Netflix drama… Caroline and Sam were in a relationship – although the specific timeline of this is a bit of a question mark It’s true that Sam and Caroline met when working at Jane Street Capital, but while the show depicts their meet-cute as happening in 2016, no one really knows when the pair first hooked up because of how often they broke up and got back together. “They had what was by all accounts this tortuous, on-again, off-again romance,” Graham told The LA Times. “And by the end of that romance they had turned each other into two people who did the exact opposite of the thing they initially set out to do.” Anthony Boyle as Sam Bankman-Fried and Julia Garner as Caroline Ellison in The Altruists Sam and Caroline started their business for altruistic reasons, although Sam later suggested this was a ‘sham’ Caroline and Sam both believed in effective altruism, a social movement that uses data and scientific reasoning to find the most impactful ways to help masses of people. According to the BBC, Sam was interested in this movement from as early as 2013, and when he landed his trading firm job, he began donating around half of his estimated $300,000 salary to charitable causes. Once FTX had grown to become one of the biggest cryptocurrencies in the world, the team pledged more than $160m to at least 110 non-profits. However, Sam later admitted his ethically driven approach was “mostly a front” for maximising profits at his cryptocurrency business. “Some of this decade’s greatest heroes will never be known,” he said during a 2025 Vox interview. “And some of its most beloved people are basically shams.” He may have called his altruism a “sham”, but The Altruists’ showrunner had faith in the couple’s intentions. The real Sam Bankman-Fried in July 2023 “I genuinely believe that when Sam and Caroline first met, they were committed, earnest altruists,” Graham Moore told TV Insider last month. “They’d gone into finance to give away as much money as possible to charity. They were both vegans. They’d both really committed themselves to spending their lives trying to make the world a better place. “By the end of their relationship, they turned each other into people who did the opposite. That’s the story we tell, and that’s the one that utterly breaks my heart.” Caroline attended a bachelorette party with a reporter, although the show didn’t quite portray this exactly as it happened In one scene from The Altruists, Caroline is seen attending a bachelorette party for one of her long-time friends. One of the other women at this party was Hannah Miller, a Bloomberg reporter, who recorded a drunken Caroline, ultimately kickstarting the investigation into FTX and Alameda. “I am not remotely a good enough writer to have made up that bachelorette party story,” Graham told the LA Times. “That is the most well-documented part of this entire thing.” Caroline is depicted in the show as being unaware of Hannah’s job, but in reality, Graham admits that the journalist did disclose her work to other guests at the party. He added: “Caroline certainly got drunk and let things slip at that bachelorette party. Had she not done that, things would have ended up very differently.” Caroline Ellison Caroline was a Harry Potter fan, just not quite to the extent depicted in the show In The Altruists, Caroline is frequently shown reading and writing Harry Potter fan-fiction. In the last episode, this pastime is even mocked in the press, alongside her conviction. The reality was that Caroline was, indeed, a Harry Potter fan who frequently posted about the franchise on her Tumblr blog and in her uncovered diary. But even though she certainly posted a lot about the boy wizard and referenced fan-fic, there is no evidence she penned any stories herself. Her One Direction obsession was also invented by the writers of the show, as she never once publicly mentioned the pop band. Caroline was interested in polyamory – but was not in a polycue with Sam In The Altruists, Caroline is seen suggesting to Sam that they be in an open relationship. This plot was once again inspired by Caroline’s notorious Tumblr account, in which she expressed an interest in polyamory. “When I first started my first foray into poly, I thought of it as a radical break from my trad past,” she wrote in 2020, as reported by The Guardian. “But tbh, I’ve come to decide the only acceptable style of poly is best characterised as something like ‘imperial Chinese harem’. None of this non-hierarchical bullshit. “Everyone should have a ranking of their partners, people should know where they fall on the ranking, and there should be vicious power struggles for the ranks.” The Altruists premiered on Netflix earlier this week Graham wondered to the LA Times: “Do we assume that she believed everything she says she believed on the blog, or do we think that sometimes when you’re a young person you write things online to try and see how you feel about it? “It’s possible she was more committed to the intellectual concept of polyamory than to its practice in her own personal life. We don’t suggest that she sleeps with terribly many more people than Sam.” Sam previously denied reports that he was in a polyamorous relationship with Caroline during a 2022 appearance on Good Morning America. Caroline toyed with the balance sheets to hide the business’ mistakes In the second episode of The Altruists, Caroline puts together technically accurate – yet financially misleading – balance sheets. During Sam Bankman-Fried’s October 2023 fraud trial, Caroline testified that she prepared seven alternative balance sheets in June 2022 to conceal Alameda’s financial risk from lenders. She disclosed that she hid that Alameda was borrowing about $10 billion from FTX customers in June 2022, when the cryptocurrency market was plummeting. “I didn’t really want to be dishonest, but I also didn’t want them to know the truth,” she said about hiding the truth from Alameda’s lenders. FTX hosted extravagant conferences in the Bahamas with guests like Bill Clinton FTX executives spent their money and time on luxury hotel stays, private planes and yachts, as well as hosting huge conferences. Some of their most famous panellists and performers over the years included Bill Clinton, Tom Brady and Liam Payne. “The FTX beach party conference that happened in the spring of 2022 was so insane,” Graham Moore told Business Insider. “Had I wanted to make up any of the details that you see about that on the show, I am not nearly creative enough to have done so.” The Bahamas plays a huge role in Sam’s life, as the CEO was arrested there in 2022. Sam didn’t try to remove Caroline from Alameda Research, but she did try to quit The Altruists charts the highs and lows of Caroline Ellison and Sam Bankman-Fried's business endeavours – and personal relationship In the series, Sam stabs Caroline in the back and tries to push her out of her company, Alameda Research. When she finds out about this, she tries to pull the same move in return and kick Sam out of his own company. Ultimately, though, their love for each other stops their mutual betrayal. This detail appears to be totally imagined for The Altruists, and did not happen in real life. In fact, Caroline testified during his trial that she tried to quit Alameda just months before FTX collapsed. “[Sam] told me I couldn’t [quit],” Carline testified, per Business Insider. “I was too important to quit.” Sam’s parents were part of a civil lawsuit involving their son’s company Throughout The Altruists, Sam’s dad Joseph is reluctant to join his company, eventually becoming an FTX advisor in the last two episodes, although he avoids getting too involved in proceedings. While Sam told the New York Times in 2022 that his parents’ involvement was “irrelevant,” the legal system did not agree. Forbes reported that Joseph and Barbara had to explain more than $26 million (£19 million) in cash and luxury properties that they “fraudulently transferred and misappropriated”. Their employers, Stanford University, even enjoyed millions in gifts from FTX-related companies. According to a civil suit filed by FTX in 2023, Sam’s parents were accused of running and benefitting from their son’s crypto empire. FTX ultimately dropped its case against Sam’s parents, and they maintained their innocence. Caroline and Sam were both jailed for their work at FTX In real life, Sam was convicted of two counts of wire fraud, two counts of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit securities fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit commodities fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering. The MIT grad was sentenced to 25 years in prison in March 2024, which he is still serving in a low-security federal prison in California. Meanwhile, Caroline was sentenced to 24 months in prison after testifying against her former partner. She served just under 10 months in jail, which she spent writing a novel and co-authoring a maths textbook. While her decade-long ban from serving as an officer or director of any public traded company is still in place, Caroline now works for a nonprofit organisation that helps charity founders find potential donors The Altruists is out now on Netflix.

articles.title: Qualcomm Celebrates Make in Africa Finale & Announces Social Impact Fund Winner
articles.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa, November 20, 2026 /3BL/ - Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. today announced the conclusion of the fourth annual Qualcomm Make in Africa Startup Mentorship Program, which culminated in its first in-person Finale at Africa Tech Festival in Cape Town. Qualcomm also announced the winner of the 2026 Qualcomm for Good Social Impact Fund. Highlights: The 2026 program supported ten startups from nine African countries developing embodied AI and edge-computing solutions across agriculture, fish-farming, e-mobility, water purification and accessibility. Qualikeeper Investments Ltd. was selected as the 2026 Qualcomm for Good Social Impact Fund winner in recognition of its affordable edge-AIoT livestock intelligence platform, StocKeeper. Applications for Qualcomm Make in Africa 2027 are now open. Applicants can visit the Qualcomm website to apply. The Finale brought the 2026 cohort together in Cape Town, where founders from across the continent presented their work as the culmination of the program. Their solutions span embodied AI and edge computing, built on Qualcomm technologies and Arduino development platforms. The equity-free program supports early-stage African technology startups through business coaching, engineering support and intellectual property guidance. The 2026 cohort worked with Qualcomm® technologies and Arduino® development platforms, including the Arduino® UNO™ Q. Through L2Pro Africa and specialist consultation from Adams & Adams, participants gained practical support to protect and commercialize their innovations. Upon completion of the program, startups will also receive a US$5,000 stipend and reimbursement of up to US$5,000 for one full utility patent application. “The Qualcomm Make in Africa program reflects the strength of Africa’s growing innovation ecosystem and the extraordinary potential and achievements of its entrepreneurs,” said Wassim Chourbaji, SVP and President of Europe, Middle East & Africa (EMEA), Qualcomm France S.A.R.L. “By providing access to Qualcomm technologies, Arduino’s development platforms, mentorship, and ecosystem support, we help founders transform bold ideas into scalable embodied AI solutions that deliver real-world impact in a cost- and energy-efficient manner. Through the Social Impact Fund, we are proud to support a startup whose innovation demonstrates exceptional promise to improve lives and create lasting social and economic impact across Africa.” “The ten startups in this year’s Qualcomm Make in Africa cohort are demonstrating how machine learning and edge technologies can be applied to solve practical challenges across a wide range of industries,” said Sudeepto Roy, Vice President of Engineering, Qualcomm Incorporated. “Throughout the program, they have advanced their prototypes while developing a stronger understanding of intellectual property and the path from invention to commercialization. Their progress is an exciting example of the technical talent and entrepreneurial ambition emerging across Africa.” Government and industry partners also underscored the program's role in advancing connectivity and local innovation across the continent. Through the 2026 Abuja Declaration on Meaningful Connectivity for Africa, ATU Member States have reaffirmed their collective commitment to accelerating digital inclusion and ensuring that all Africans can meaningfully participate in the digital economy. The innovators selected for this year's Qualcomm Make in Africa cohort demonstrate how this vision can be translated into tangible impact, harnessing artificial intelligence, advanced connectivity and other emerging technologies to develop locally relevant solutions that address real-world challenges and improve lives across African communities," said Martial Dhossa, Deputy Director, Radiocommunications, African Telecommunications Union (ATU). Qualcomm for Good Social Impact Fund winner: The Qualcomm for Good Social Impact Fund gives one startup from each Qualcomm Make in Africa cohort a grant to support an especially compelling social impact use case, helping it further develop and deploy its solution, measure its impact and accelerate scale. Qualikeeper was announced as the winner of the 2026 Qualcomm for Good Social Impact Fund. It will receive an equity-free US$75,000 grant and tailored technical support to help scale its solution and expand its impact. “Qualikeeper was selected in recognition of its vision, ingenuity and dedication to strengthening animal health and farmer livelihoods among livestock-dependent communities in resource constrained environments. By combining technological innovation with a clear focus on real-world impact, the team is demonstrating the potential of African entrepreneurship to address important challenges and create lasting value for communities,” said Erica Ciaraldi, Manager, Government Affairs, Qualcomm Incorporated. “We are delighted to recognize their achievements through the Qualcomm for Good Social Impact Fund. We look forward to seeing how they continue to grow their AIoT livestock monitoring system, reach new communities and expand their impact across Africa and beyond.” Looking ahead: Qualcomm Make in Africa Startup Mentorship Program 2027 Building on the success of the program, applications for the 2027 Qualcomm Make in Africa Startup Mentorship Program are now open. Further information and application details are available at: https://www.qualcomm.com/company/locations/africa/qualcomm-make-in-africa About Qualcomm Qualcomm relentlessly innovates to deliver intelligent computing everywhere, helping the world tackle some of its most important challenges. Building on our 40 years of technology leadership in creating era-defining breakthroughs, we deliver a broad portfolio of solutions built with our leading-edge AI, high-performance, low-power computing and unrivaled connectivity. Our Snapdragon® platforms power extraordinary consumer experiences, and our Qualcomm Dragonwing™ products empower businesses and industries to scale to new heights. Together with our ecosystem partners, we enable next-generation digital transformation to enrich lives, improve businesses, and advance societies. Qualcomm Incorporated includes our licensing business, QTL, and the vast majority of our patent portfolio. Qualcomm Technologies, Inc., a subsidiary of Qualcomm Incorporated, operates, along with its subsidiaries, substantially all of our engineering and research and development functions and substantially all of our products and services businesses, including our QCT semiconductor business.
